title: Basel III: Finalising post-crisis reforms
summary: The Basel Committee on Banking Supervision published this document in December 2017 to finalize the Basel III framework, addressing shortcomings in pre-crisis regulatory architecture and reducing excessive variability in risk-weighted assets (RWAs). The revisions enhance standardized approaches for credit and operational risk, constrain internal-modelled approaches, and implement a finalised leverage ratio with a capital floor.
key_points: Document finalizes Basel III post-crisis reforms, complementing earlier Basel III phases, with implementation phased from January 2022 through January 2027
Key objective is reducing excessive RWA variability that eroded confidence in banks' reported risk-weighted capital ratios during the global financial crisis
Revisions include enhanced standardised approaches for credit risk and operational risk to improve comparability of banks' capital ratios
Output floor implementation is phased: 50% (Jan 2022), increasing by 5% annually to 72.5% (Jan 2027)
Leverage ratio includes revised exposure definition with G-SIB buffer effective January 2022
Jurisdictions may implement more conservative requirements or accelerated transitional arrangements as Basel constitutes minimum standards
why_it_matters: This regulatory framework directly affects how banks calculate capital requirements, influencing their risk-taking behavior, lending capacity, and competitive dynamics. Banks' RWA calculations must be more transparent and comparable, enabling market participants and supervisors to better assess systemic risk. The phased implementation (2022-2027) provides orderly transition while strengthening the resilience of the banking system.
market_structure_context: This document establishes the final Basel III post-crisis regulatory architecture. Key structural elements include: (1) output floor limiting the benefit banks can claim from internal models versus standardised approaches, (2) finalised leverage ratio as a non-risk-based backstop, (3) constraints on internal ratings-based (IRB) approaches for credit risk, and (4) revised CVA framework for counterparty credit risk. These measures directly address market structure concerns about RWA variability and model arbitrage that contributed to the financial crisis.
important_numbers: Revised leverage ratio exposure definition effective: 1 January 2022
